sources.title: National Register of Historic Places listings in Hennepin County, Minnesota

stops.name: Guthrie Theater
stops.description: A cobalt-blue theater whose cantilevered Endless Bridge juts out over the river with a free public view toward the falls.

stops.name: Gold Medal Park
stops.description: A gently spiraling grassy mound on the riverfront, named for the Gold Medal flour once milled next door.

stops.name: Mill City Museum
stops.description: Built into the ruins of the Washburn A Mill, once the largest flour mill in the world, telling how milling made the city.

stops.name: Mill Ruins Park
stops.description: Excavated foundations and tailrace canals of the vanished flour mills lie exposed at the west edge of the falls.

stops.name: Stone Arch Bridge
stops.description: The only stone arch bridge on the Mississippi, a former rail crossing that now carries walkers across the face of the falls.

stops.name: Saint Anthony Falls
stops.description: The only major waterfall on the Mississippi, the water power that turned Minneapolis into the flour-milling capital of the world.

stops.name: Pillsbury A-Mill
stops.description: For forty years the largest flour mill on earth, its limestone towers driven by two of the most powerful waterwheels ever built.

stops.name: Our Lady of Lourdes Catholic Church
stops.description: The oldest continuously used church in Minneapolis, begun in 1856 and finished by a French Canadian congregation.

stops.name: Ard Godfrey House
stops.description: The oldest surviving wood-frame house in Minneapolis, home of the millwright who ran the first sawmill at the falls.

stops.name: Grain Belt Beer Sign
stops.description: A giant 1940s neon bottle cap on Nicollet Island, once one of the largest neon signs in the country and a beloved landmark.

stops.name: Nicollet Island
stops.description: A wooded island in the middle of the Mississippi carrying Victorian houses, a park, and long views back toward the falls.

stops.name: Merriam Street Bridge
stops.description: A wrought-iron bridge salvaged from a downtown crossing that now links Nicollet Island to the east bank on foot.

stops.name: Hennepin Avenue Bridge
stops.description: A suspension bridge named for Father Louis Hennepin, the explorer who first reported the falls to Europeans in 1680.

note: A tight riverfront loop through the St. Anthony Falls Historic District, the milling core the city grew from, crossing on the Stone Arch Bridge and returning over Merriam Street and Hennepin Avenue bridges. Gold Medal Park, Mill Ruins Park, the Stone Arch Bridge, the falls, Nicollet Island, the Grain Belt sign and both return bridges have no street-number address, so they carry article coordinates and a null address rather than a guessed one. Mill Ruins Park is included by coordinates because 102 Portland Ave S geocodes to the far south end of that avenue, not the river. Downtown icons a little off the loop (Foshay Tower, First Avenue, IDS Center, Minneapolis City Hall, Nicollet Mall) were left out to keep the walk to about a mile; they are strong candidates for a separate downtown loop.
